html:
Argentine general who led the fight for independence in the south of South America. He is the national hero of Argentina and is also honoured in Chile and Peru.

Born in a small town on the Uruguay River, he grew up in Spain and fought in the Spanish army against Napoleon's invasion. In 1812 he sailed to Buenos Aires to join the wars of independence.

His plan was to strike Spain's stronghold, Peru, by way of Chile:

  • In 1817 he led the Army of the Andes over mountain passes more than 4,000 metres high.
  • With Bernardo O'Higgins he won at Chacabuco in 1817 and Maipú in 1818, freeing Chile.
  • In 1820 he sailed to Peru, and in 1821 he declared its independence in Lima.

In 1822 he met Simón Bolívar at Guayaquil. No one knows exactly what they said, but afterwards San Martín stepped aside and left Bolívar to finish the war. He spent his last decades in Europe and died in France in 1850.
